o1.biggest_strength: It nails the three signals — agency-only Semrush losses, the self-inflicted Lite usage cliff, and the under-nurtured multi-site free accounts — and ranks the Lite fix within the top two with a concrete A/B test.
o1.biggest_mistake: Move 5 ('Teach with our link data') has no real number behind it and reads like the generic content advice the owner said would annoy them; the success metric (in-house trial share rising) is not plausibly attributable to one blog study.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace Move 5 with a harder-lever move (or cut to four), and tighten the per-100-trial math table so the working is unambiguous in one line.

o2.biggest_strength: It leads with a clear 'position to own' (the data SEOs trust, wrapped in the Monday report), shows its working transparently (churn weighting, trial-loss math, survey margin), and explicitly separates what it is sure and unsure about.
o2.biggest_mistake: Move 1 commits to a rising target (15%) and the move set is slightly safer — Move 5 again drifts into vague content marketing with a soft metric rather than a hard lever like the multi-site or top-up test.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Swap the weakest move for a sharper commercial lever and add one non-obvious insight the owner hadn't already flagged, rather than tuning the known ones.

reason: Both get the three signals and the 'don't chase PPC' call right, but Output 2's transparent working, careful survey-margin handling and explicit 'what this is built from / to confirm' make it the version I'd actually forward. Output 1's Move 5 is the one bit I'd bin.
